rationale: The three relationship types the Visual Basic lane had no verdict for at handover. Each is a GAP and not a ruling, because VB HAS the construct; the corpus measurement that says so is in script/m14/vb-ontology-census.ts over 2,658 tracked .vb files (p3d, dismt, pcl, tankex, runtime). (1) `exports`: VB expresses export through ACCESSIBILITY, not through a keyword. `exports_statement`, `export_list` and `assembly_attribute` are node types the grammar HAS RULES for and that occur ZERO times in 2,658 files, so a keyword-shaped `exports` in VB would be an edge the language cannot express -- which is why the verdict rests on a MODIFIER count (15,489 `public` modifiers in 2,344 files) and on the documented default-accessibility table (136 modifier-less members in a class, 20 in a module, 5 in a structure, 116 modifier-less top-level types), not on a node-type count. (2) `instantiates`: four VB construction surfaces, four shapes -- `object_creation_expression` (1,612 standalone), `array_creation_expression` (15,181 standalone), `as_clause` beginning `As New` (2,499), and a QUALIFIED construction whose `New` head is only the leading segment of an access chain (15,233 + 310 fragments). The last one is the common case in this grammar and the one that fabricates a target if read naively. (3) `uses`: 323,540 `member_access_expression` and 1,017 `with_member_access_expression` nodes are a name READ rather than a callee or an index, in 1,921 of 2,658 files. This file also pins FOUR defects found while establishing those verdicts, all of them invisible to a corpus-wide count because the counts stayed healthy: a construction published as `calls` (a `New` in the call graph), `Protected Friend` read as `internal` (one `member_modifier` node holding two words), the header clause branch dead because `headerColonIndex` compared subtree ids instead of document positions (both header clauses in the corpus published NO heritage edge), and `visibility` falling through to `internal` where VB's own table says a modifier-less Procedure/Property/Event defaults to Public. The expectation pins `meta.evidenceClass` on one edge of every class and `meta.accessLevel` / `meta.accessFromModifier` on the accessibility rows, because two of the eleven injected mutants survived a fixture that asserted only the edge's existence: an analyzer that stamped no evidence class at all, and one that read a combined `member_modifier` as a single opaque token (which empties the access-level set and silently falls back to the default table, so `Protected Friend` would have looked exported for the wrong reason). Both are dead assertions until the metadata is pinned.

expectRelationships.comment: NO ACCESS MODIFIER, PROCEDURE: VB's documented default for a Procedure/Property/Event is PUBLIC, not Private. A modifier-less `Sub` in a Class IS callable from another assembly. The old fall-through published this `internal`.

THE COMBINED MODIFIER. `Protected Friend` is 'protected OR friend', so it IS assembly-reachable through the friend half. This grammar puts the two words in ONE `member_modifier` node, so reading its text verbatim produced the single token 'protected friend', which matched no entry in the visibility order and fell through to `internal` -- 12 declarations on the lane corpus, every one wrong. accessLevel is the SET, joined.
an explicitly Public FIELD

THE CONTAINER IS OBSERVABLE. A modifier-less field is Private in a Class or Module and PUBLIC in a Structure, so `X` in `Coord` is an export while `_implicitPrivate` in `Api` is not. Same rule, opposite answer, one line apart in the file.
a modifier-less PROCEDURE in a MODULE: default Public

A modifier-less top-level CLASS defaults to `Friend`, so `InternalOnly` is not an export of the assembly (`root -> InternalOnly` is in forbidRelationships) while its Public member still is, carrying `ownerAccessLevel: friend`. The edge is not suppressed by the container's visibility: a `Friend` type is assembly-visible to a FRIEND ASSEMBLY, which is per-project configuration this analyzer never sees.
an interface member: default Public

CONSTRUCTION SURFACE 4: `As New T()`. The `New` keyword is inlined away by the grammar's `as_clause` rule -- 0 of 30,001 as_clause nodes carry an `As` or `New` token -- so this is a word-bounded char scan of the node's own span. `As New Timers.Timer()` puts an `array_type` in `declared_type` because the `()` reads as bounds, so the target is the ELEMENT type.
a GENERIC `As New`: the target is `List`, not the type argument `String`. `calleeLeaf` skips a `type_argument_list`, the same exclusion the heritage path and every other name in this analyzer apply.

CONSTRUCTION SURFACE 1: `New Foo()` with an EMPTY argument list is an `object_creation_expression`. It is `instantiates`, not `calls` -- publishing both would put one syntactic event in the call graph twice.

CONSTRUCTION SURFACE 2: `New Foo(1, 2)` with arguments is an `array_creation_expression` with a `type` field and a `bounds` field and NO `function` field. Keying on `invocation_expression` alone dropped every one of these: 15,181 on the lane corpus, in 1,687 of 2,658 files.

CONSTRUCTION SURFACE 4: a QUALIFIED construction. `New System.Drawing.Size(3, 4)` does not parse as one construction -- the `object_creation_expression` holds only `New System` and the type is the LAST leaf of the enclosing access chain. Publishing that node's own `type` field gave `instantiates -> System`, a namespace nobody constructs: the grammar's fragmentation turned into a fact about the program.
a construction in a RETURN, so the enclosing declaration is the source
the same qualified-construction rule reached through the `As New` surface

`New System.Drawing.Size(3, 4)`: `Drawing` is a member-access segment in a VALUE slot -- nothing is invoked on it -- so it is a read. Its sibling `System` is the `New` head of the construction and is neither a read nor a target.

the last segment of the same chain, in a VALUE slot because nothing is invoked on it. With `UTF8()` there would be a `calls` edge instead and no `uses` edge: the callee slot is excluded so the two classes are disjoint.
the middle segment of the same chain: a TYPE name, and a read of it

a NAMESPACE segment of a three-segment access chain. The tree cannot tell a namespace segment from a member of the same name, so the edge is labelled `uses` -- a read of a NAME -- and carries no claim about what kind of member it is.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE HEADER CLAUSE. `Class C : Inherits B` is an `extends`, decided by reading the `Inherits` keyword out of the source span between the `:` and the first name -- the grammar inlines the keyword away, so the node types alone cannot tell `Inherits` from `Implements`. THE WHOLE HEADER BRANCH WAS DEAD before this wave: `headerColonIndex` compared node `id`s, and a web-tree-sitter `id` is an internal subtree pointer rather than a document position, so the `:` was never found. Both header clauses in the 2,658-file corpus published no heritage edge at all.

THE KEYWORD-LESS INTERFACE HEADER. `Interface I : IDisposable` has no `Inherits`/`Implements` keyword at all, and VB has no interface inheritance, so every entry is an interface the type IMPLEMENTS. Labelled `extends`, which is the mislabel a single `seenInherits = -1` flag produced.
the second entry of the same keyword-less list -- every entry gets its own edge, and none of them is `extends`

forbidRelationships.comment: A modifier-less top-level CLASS defaults to `Friend`, which is assembly-INTERNAL. The type is not part of the assembly's public surface, and its member still is (see `InternalOnly -> LooksPublic`, which records `ownerAccessLevel: friend`).

SUPERSEDES an earlier `uses QualifiedRead -> _name` row. `Me._name = "x"` (line 183) ASSIGNS a member: the name is written, not read, and `uses` is the family’s value-read class (go’s GO1 and csharp’s CS-D4/CS-R1 define it as a read that is neither a call nor a write). This analyzer publishes no `writes` edges at all, so the write is a DISCLOSED GAP rather than a represented fact — but absorbing it into `uses` would not fill the gap, it would mislabel a mutation as a read and make the two classes overlap on one expression. Keeping the old row is the failure mode this forbid exists to catch.
control: `Friend` alone is assembly-internal, NOT exported. The pair with `BothHalves` is what makes `Protected Friend` a fact rather than 'any modifier at all'.
control: `Protected` alone is subclass-only, NOT assembly-exported -- the same modifier family as `BothHalves` with the opposite answer.
control: a modifier-less FIELD defaults to Private. This is the row that separates the field default from the procedure default, and `Coord -> X` is the same rule with the opposite answer.
control: an explicitly Private field in a Structure is not exported, even though a modifier-less one is
control: a modifier-less FIELD in a MODULE is Private. A Module's default is a PROCEDURE default, so `Helpers -> Go` is exported and this is not.
control: an edge to a name no declaration writes

PRE-FIX SHAPE for the qualified construction: the `object_creation_expression` holds only `New System`, so reading its own `type` field publishes a NAMESPACE as the constructed type. The grammar's fragmentation must not become a fact about the program.
control: a generic type ARGUMENT is not what is constructed. `As New List(Of String)` constructs `List`; `String` is an argument.
PRE-FIX SHAPE: constructions were published under `calls`, which put a constructor invocation in the call graph and double-counted one syntactic event under two labels.
the same for the argument-less construction surface
control: `sb.Append("x")` puts `Append` in the CALLEE slot, so it is a `calls` target and not a `uses` target. Publishing both labels for one name would make the two classes indistinguishable.
control: the same exclusion for `Me.GetHashCode()`, where the grammar puts the member access in the `function` field of an `invocation_expression`
control: `System` is the RECEIVER of the access chain, written as a bare identifier rather than a member access. The edge is the member name of a qualified access, and a bare receiver names nothing.
PRE-FIX SHAPE for the keyword-less interface header: labelled `extends`. VB has no interface inheritance, so every entry of `Interface I : IDisposable` is an interface the type IMPLEMENTS.

control: a VB KEYWORD is never a heritage target. Where the grammar leaves the keyword in the tree, `Implements` parsed as a `simple_name` and the analyzer would have published `extends entry_ -> Implements`.

knownResidual: `uses` targets are the NAME the file reads and not a resolved symbol: a qualified read usually names a member of a type this file does not declare, so the edge resolves at both ends about as often as a `calls` edge does (12.0% measured over the corpus's `calls` population) and that is the honest number for a cross-file name rather than a defect. `uses` is deduplicated per (source, target) keeping the first site, with the raw site count on `metadata.sites`, which matches the family's own `uses` emission (csharp keys on `source::uses::name`). A dotted path publishes one edge per SEGMENT the file reads, so `A.B.C` yields `uses` on `B` and on `C`, and `B` may be a namespace segment rather than a member -- the tree cannot tell, and the edge therefore claims only that the name is read. Separately, VB's grammar gives an unqualified call `Foo(x)` and an index `xs(i)` the SAME node type (`array_access_expression`), so this analyzer publishes neither as `calls`: 24,804 identifier-headed and 74,482 member-access-headed sites on the corpus have no call edge, and a heuristic that guessed which was which would be a guess published as fact. That gap is measured and declared rather than filled.
